checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is DataColumnSidecarsByRange response ordering deterministic?

audit_items.state_context: sortedUniqueBlocks() inside canonicalFilter.filter() sorts blocks by slot. wantedColumns is sorted before passing to streamDataColumnBatch. Duplicate column indices in request.Columns are NOT deduplicated.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The response ordering is MOSTLY deterministic: (1) blocks are sorted by slot via sortedUniqueBlocks in canonicalFilter.filter; (2) wantedColumns is sorted via slices.Sort at line 94. However, duplicate column indices in request.Columns are propagated into wantedColumns without deduplication. After sorting, e.g., [1,1,2] remains [1,1,2], causing storage.Get to be called with duplicate indices, potentially streaming the same sidecar twice.
invariants_identified: wantedColumns is sorted ascending before use
Blocks are returned in ascending slot order from batcher
Duplicate column indices in request are not removed

phase2.symbolic_execution: Trace: request.Columns=[1,1,2] -> wantedColumns=[1,1,2] (copy+sort) -> streamDataColumnBatch called with [1,1,2] -> storage.Get(root, [1,1,2]) -> if storage returns col1,col1,col2 (duplicates), all are streamed -> peer receives 3 chunks for block, 2 of which are identical sidecar index 1.

counterexamples.outcome: wantedColumns = [1,1,2,3] after sort; same sidecar for column 1 streamed twice per block; quota consumed twice for column 1

phase2_5.additional_vectors: A separate resource leak exists: ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Second) at line 80 is never stopped (no defer ticker.Stop()), unlike rpc_blob_sidecars_by_range.go:90 which has defer ticker.Stop(). Under high request rates, many orphaned tickers accumulate.
phase2_5.attack_surface: Any P2P peer can send DataColumnSidecarsByRangeRequest with duplicate column indices to trigger redundant streaming.

phase3.invariant_proving: The ordering invariant holds in the absence of duplicate indices. With duplicates, the ordering is still deterministic but redundant. The spec (Ethereum Fulu p2p-interface) does not explicitly prohibit duplicate column indices in requests, so the server should either reject or deduplicate them.
phase3.proof_or_counterexample: Counterexample for completeness violation: request.Columns=[0,0] causes column 0 to be streamed twice. Ordering property still holds (0,0 in order), but response does not match unique-sidecar semantics.

phase3_5.severity_calibration: Low-Medium. The duplicate handling is a protocol ambiguity that wastes quota and may confuse requestors, but does not cause security violations. The ticker leak is the more impactful finding.
phase3_5.exploitability: Any connected peer can trigger; no special permissions needed.

audit_items.vulnerability_description: Duplicate column indices in DataColumnSidecarsByRange requests are not deduplicated, causing redundant streaming and quota waste. Additionally, the ticker created at line 80 is never stopped (resource leak).
audit_items.reasoning: The ordering invariant holds. The duplicate issue is a correctness/efficiency concern. The ticker leak is a resource management bug. Neither constitutes a direct security boundary violation, but the ticker leak is exploitable for resource exhaustion at low severity.
audit_items.recommended_fix: 1. Deduplicate request.Columns before copying into wantedColumns. 2. Add 'defer ticker.Stop()' immediately after 'ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Second)' at line 80.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange include ALL sidecars from a block when any is included?

audit_items.state_context: quota decrements per-sidecar. Early return when quota==0 can occur mid-block, between streaming first and last sidecar for a given block.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The function iterates blocks (outer loop) and sidecars (inner loop), decrementing quota after each sidecar write. The early-exit condition 'if quota == 0 { return 0, nil }' is evaluated INSIDE the inner sidecar loop. This means quota can reach zero after streaming k < len(wantedDataColumnIndices) sidecars for a block, leaving the remainder unstreamned. The requesting peer receives a partial set for that block.
invariants_identified: Early exit occurs inside inner loop (mid-block)
Spec intent: if a block is included, ALL requested columns for it must be included

phase2.symbolic_execution: Concrete trace: MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars=10, wantedColumns=[0,1,2,3] (4 columns). Block A: streams 4 sidecars (quota: 10->6). Block B: streams 4 sidecars (quota: 6->2). Block C: streams column[0] (quota: 2->1), streams column[1] (quota: 1->0) -> EARLY EXIT. Result: peer receives columns [0,1] for Block C but not [2,3]. Peer cannot reconstruct Block C data reliably.

counterexamples.inputs: MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars=10, request.Columns=[0,1,2,3], Count >= 3 blocks each with 4 available sidecars
counterexamples.outcome: Block C receives only columns 0 and 1 instead of all 4 requested. Violation of atomicity per block.

phase2_5.additional_vectors: Any peer can craft a request to trigger this: choose Count and Columns such that MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars % len(Columns) != 0. The 3rd-to-last block will always receive a partial sidecar set.
phase2_5.attack_surface: Peer requesting data may receive incomplete sidecar set per block, making erasure coding reconstruction impossible for the partial block.

phase3.invariant_proving: The invariant 'all sidecars for included block must be served' FAILS. Proof: Let N = MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars, K = len(wantedColumns). If N mod K != 0, then after floor(N/K) complete blocks, the (floor(N/K)+1)th block will have only (N mod K) sidecars served. This is a provably reachable state for any K that does not evenly divide N.
phase3.proof_or_counterexample: N=16384 (mainnet), K=3: 16384 mod 3 = 1. The 5462nd block will receive only 1 out of 3 requested sidecars. Deterministically triggerable.

phase3_5.severity_calibration: Medium. Causes incomplete sidecar delivery per block. Peers expecting complete data for each block will fail reconstruction. Aligned with Fulu spec requirement that block sidecar delivery must be atomic per block.
phase3_5.exploitability: Deterministically triggerable by any P2P peer with a correctly crafted request. No authentication needed.

audit_items.vulnerability_description: streamDataColumnBatch can return mid-block when quota is exhausted, violating the Fulu spec requirement that if any sidecar for a block is served, all requested sidecars for that block must be served. This is deterministically triggerable when MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars is not evenly divisible by the number of requested columns.
audit_items.reasoning: The quota decrement occurs per-sidecar inside the inner loop, with early exit on quota==0 without block-boundary awareness. The Fulu spec requires per-block atomicity of sidecar delivery. This is a confirmed violation.
audit_items.recommended_fix: Before beginning to stream sidecars for a block, check if quota >= len(wantedDataColumnIndices). If not, break the outer loop without streaming any sidecars for that block. Change: add a pre-check 'if quota < uint64(len(wantedDataColumnIndices)) { return quota, nil }' before the inner sidecar loop.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Are DataColumnSidecarsByRange responses from the canonical fork choice chain?

audit_items.state_context: IsCanonical delegates to blockchain service. canonicalFilter maintains prevRoot across batches. Non-linear detection: if prevRoot != block.ParentRoot(), remaining blocks added to nonlin and iteration stops.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: Two-layer defense: (1) IsCanonical filters non-canonical blocks per-block; (2) parent chain linearity check prevents mixed-fork serving even if fork choice changes mid-stream. The canonicalFilter.prevRoot state persists across batch boundaries, maintaining chain continuity.
invariants_identified: Parent chain linear check across batch boundaries via prevRoot
Non-linear detection triggers immediate stream stop

phase2.symbolic_execution: Attack attempt: During a long-range request spanning multiple batches, fork choice reorganizes between batch K and batch K+1. At batch K+1, new canonical chain has different blocks. IsCanonical now returns false for the old chain blocks. canonicalFilter.filter excludes them. If a new canonical block exists that is not a child of prevRoot, the parent chain check fires, setting nonlin and stopping iteration. The stream is cleanly terminated without serving non-canonical data.

phase2_5.additional_vectors: TOCTOU consideration: between IsCanonical check and actual streaming, a reorg could theoretically make a block non-canonical. However, since the data is already fetched and the IsCanonical check already confirmed, the served data is correct for the state at time of check. The stream abort on non-linear detection provides an additional safety net.
phase2_5.attack_surface: No exploitable path found for serving non-canonical data.

phase3.invariant_proving: The invariant 'all served blocks are from canonical chain' holds under both steady state and reorg scenarios. The parent chain linearity check provides defense-in-depth beyond IsCanonical.
phase3.proof_or_counterexample: No counterexample found after exhaustive scenario analysis including: reorg mid-stream, slow reorg, equivocation attacks, long-range rewrites.

phase3_5.severity_calibration: Not a vulnerability. The guard is sufficient for all scenarios analyzed.

audit_items.reasoning: The combination of IsCanonical check and parent chain linearity check (canonicalFilter) provides robust defense against serving non-canonical data. The prevRoot state persists across batch boundaries, preventing mixed-fork responses even during reorgs. No concrete counterexample found.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is data_column_serve_range correctly enforced?

audit_items.state_context: FuluEnabled() returns true when FuluForkEpoch < math.MaxUint64. MinEpochsForDataColumnSidecarsRequest defines how far back serving is required. The outer guard currEpoch > minReqEpochs prevents uint64 underflow before the subtraction.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The function enforces minimum slot for serving: the guard 'currEpoch > minReqEpochs' prevents underflow. When Fulu is not enabled, MaxUint64 is returned, ensuring no data is served (since no real slot can be >= MaxUint64). The condition 'currEpoch-minReqEpochs > minStartEpoch' ensures minStartEpoch is only advanced when mathematically safe.
invariants_identified: FuluEnabled() guard prevents pre-Fulu data serving
minStartEpoch only advances when result > FuluForkEpoch

phase2.symbolic_execution: Underflow test: currEpoch=5, minReqEpochs=10. Condition 'currEpoch > minReqEpochs' is false (5 > 10 is false). minStartEpoch stays at FuluForkEpoch. No underflow. Off-by-one test: currEpoch=FuluForkEpoch+minReqEpochs, condition: currEpoch > minReqEpochs is true, currEpoch-minReqEpochs = FuluForkEpoch, condition 'currEpoch-minReqEpochs > minStartEpoch' is 'FuluForkEpoch > FuluForkEpoch' = false. minStartEpoch stays at FuluForkEpoch — serving from Fulu genesis. When currEpoch = FuluForkEpoch+minReqEpochs+1: condition is true, minStartEpoch advances by 1.

counterexamples.scenario: Off-by-one: serves one extra epoch of history
counterexamples.outcome: Server serves from FuluForkEpoch instead of FuluForkEpoch+1. One extra epoch of historical data served. Not a security issue, just leniency.

phase2_5.additional_vectors: validateDataColumnsByRange calls dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot and computes 'if endSlot < minStartSlot { return nil }' — correctly skips too-old requests. No bypass path found.
phase2_5.attack_surface: The off-by-one allows serving one extra epoch, but this is leniency (serves MORE history than required), not a restriction bypass. No attack vector.

phase3.invariant_proving: The serve range restriction invariant holds: no data older than required is served beyond one epoch of leniency. The FuluEnabled guard prevents pre-Fulu serving entirely. Overflow protection is correct.
phase3.proof_or_counterexample: The only deviation is a one-epoch leniency which is a conservative (safe) direction of deviation.

phase3_5.severity_calibration: Informational. One-epoch leniency is not a security concern. All critical guards are in place.

audit_items.vulnerability_description: Minor off-by-one: server serves data starting from FuluForkEpoch (inclusive) when currEpoch == FuluForkEpoch + MinEpochsForDataColumnSidecarsRequest, whereas strict enforcement would require starting from FuluForkEpoch+1. This is a leniency, not a restriction bypass.
audit_items.reasoning: All overflow and underflow protections are correct. The FuluEnabled guard prevents pre-Fulu data serving. The one-epoch leniency is a conservative deviation (serves more history than strictly required by the spec), not a security issue.
audit_items.recommended_fix: For strict spec compliance, change the condition from '>' to '>=' in 'currEpoch-minReqEpochs > minStartEpoch'.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot reject requests exceeding MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS?

audit_items.state_context: validateDataColumnsByRootRequest counts total column entries including duplicates. Handler merges by root into requestedColumnsByRoot map (deduplicates block roots but NOT column indices within a root). storage.Get called with potentially duplicate column list.

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The validator counts len(id.Columns) for each identifier without deduplication. An attacker can craft a request where: (a) all column entries are duplicates of a single column index, (b) total == MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars (passes validation), (c) actual unique sidecars requested == 1 (trivial to serve). Conversely, by splitting column indices across multiple identifiers for the same root, the validator might count them as separate entries while the handler deduplicates, serving fewer sidecars than the limit would suggest. The key attack is the duplicate-inflation path.
invariants_identified: Validator counts raw list lengths (including duplicates)
Handler iterates identifiers sequentially (not deduplicated per root at validation time)
storage.Get receives the raw columns list (possibly with duplicates)
rateLimiter charges based on raw len(columns)

phase2.symbolic_execution: Attack trace: MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars = 16384. Craft request: 1 identifier with BlockRoot=R, Columns=[0, 0, 0, ..., 0] (16384 zeros). Validator: total = 16384, NOT > 16384, passes. Handler: root=R, columns=[0,0,...,0] (16384 entries). rateLimiter.add(stream, 16384). storage.Get(R, [0,0,...,0]). If storage returns 16384 copies of column 0 sidecar: 16384 sidecar chunks are written to stream (amplification). If storage deduplicates internally and returns 1 sidecar: only 1 chunk written, but rate limiter was charged 16384 (incorrect accounting). In either case, the validator-handler contract is violated.

counterexamples.scenario: Duplicate column index amplification (if storage returns duplicates)
counterexamples.outcome: Validator passes (total==16384 == limit), storage returns 16384 copies of column 0, all written to stream. Net effect: 16384 wire writes for 1 unique sidecar. Server performs maximum work for trivially small unique data.
rateLimiter charged 16384 for a request that serves only 1 unique sidecar. Rate limiter is incorrectly over-charged, consuming peer's budget without serving actual data.

Validator counts 256. Handler: requestedColumnsByRoot[R] = [0..127, 128..255] (all 256 unique). Serves 256 sidecars. This is correct behavior, but demonstrates that splitting does not bypass the limit.

phase2_5.additional_vectors: The by-root handler also lacks validation of column index values — e.g., column index >= NumberOfColumns (128 on mainnet) should be rejected but the validator only checks count. However, storage.Get will likely return empty results for out-of-range indices rather than panic.
phase2_5.attack_surface: Any P2P peer can send a malformed request with duplicate column indices to trigger maximum server-side work (up to 16384 storage lookups and writes) for a single unique sidecar.

phase3.invariant_proving: The invariant 'total unique sidecars served <= MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars' MAY hold if storage deduplicates internally, but the invariant 'server work bounded by MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars' is violated. The validator only bounds the sum of raw list lengths, not unique (block_root, column_index) pairs. For the security boundary intended by MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS (bounding server work), the current implementation is insufficient.
phase3.proof_or_counterexample: Proof of bound violation: request with duplicate columns passes validation with total==MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars. Handler calls storage.Get with duplicate list. Server performs O(MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars) storage operations for O(1) unique sidecars. This is a work amplification attack.

phase3_5.severity_calibration: Medium-High. The duplicate column attack enables a peer to cause the server to perform maximum-bounded work (storage lookups, stream writes) for minimum unique data. On mainnet with MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars=16384, this allows 16384 storage operations and stream writes per request per connection. Under connection flooding, this constitutes a DoS amplification attack bounded only by the rate limiter (which is incorrectly charged based on duplicates).
phase3_5.exploitability: High exploitability: any unauthenticated P2P peer can craft this request with no special knowledge. Impact scales with connection count.

audit_items.vulnerability_description: validateDataColumnsByRootRequest counts raw column list lengths including duplicate indices, while the Fulu spec intends MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS to bound the number of unique (block_root, column_index) pairs served. An attacker can craft a request with MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars duplicate entries for a single column index, passing validation while causing the server to perform maximum-bounded work (storage lookups, stream writes) for a single unique sidecar. This is a DoS amplification vulnerability.
audit_items.reasoning: The validator-handler contract is violated: validation bounds raw list length, but the handler processes each entry (including duplicates). Depending on storage.Get behavior with duplicate indices, the server performs O(MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars) work per request. The rate limiter is incorrectly charged based on raw (duplicate) list length rather than unique sidecar count.
audit_items.recommended_fix: 1. In validateDataColumnsByRootRequest: count unique (block_root, column_index) pairs. 2. In dataColumnSidecarByRootRPCHandler: deduplicate column indices per root before calling storage.Get. 3. Validate that column indices are within [0, NumberOfColumns) range.
